description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tweets categorized by sentiment polarity scores ranging from 0 to 5, as part of an analysis of vaccine-related sentiments during the development and deployment of COVID-19 vaccines. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of tweets,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400,000 with tick marks at intervals of 100,000. The horizontal axis displays discrete sentiment polarity values (0 through 5), with each bar representing the total number of tweets associated with that score. The bar for polarity 0 is very short, indicating near-zero tweets; polarity 1 has the tallest bar, reaching approximately 460,000 tweets and colored in brown; polarity 2 follows with a green bar at about 410,000 tweets; polarity 3 is represented by a red bar at roughly 90,000 tweets; polarity 4 is nearly flat, indicating very few tweets; and polarity 5 has no visible bar, suggesting no tweets were assigned that score. The bars are not sorted by height and are presented in ascending order of polarity score. A gray rectangular overlay partially obscures the x-axis label for polarity 3, but the numerical labels remain legible. The chart visually emphasizes that the majority of vaccine-related tweets during this period exhibited slightly positive sentiment (polarity 1 and 2), with minimal representation of neutral (0), strongly positive (3), or extreme sentiment scores (4 and 5).
